subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose explicit child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that be implemented through an accepted per-kind/core session-binding capability while keeping Telegram's default top-level placement as current?
rationale: Current main has the binding primitives, but the remaining behavior controls user-visible Telegram topic creation, plugin/API capability shape, and session/message routing defaults, which requires maintainer intent before implementation or closure.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve its ownership and visibility blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep Telegram's current-conversation binding behavior and leave this issue open until maintainers decide the child-topic API and default-visibility model.

options.title: Reject Telegram child-topic spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide subagent work should not create Telegram topics even when explicitly requested.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve its ownership and visibility blockers, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the merged core session-binding refactor and current policy/tool gate that the remaining Telegram decision must fit.
